parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing criminalisation, border, facility or screening restriction is documented, and national law protects gender identity/expression, hate-crime provisions, an X marker and identity-based custody placement. One province documents a human-rights recourse route. Offsetting this are rising police-reported hate crimes, an organised anti-trans movement, reported abuse of gender-diverse prisoners, and provincial school/health rollbacks affecting minors, with hate-crime data not disaggregated by gender identity. Overall this is reduced risk with material uncertainty, not low risk.

entry_documents.protection: National documents offer an X marker; foreign-passport entry practice is not documented.
entry_documents.interaction: No documented border screening turns a marker or presentation into detention, entry refusal or invasive search.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: A 2022 report alleged a pattern of abuse/discrimination and higher sexual-assault risk for gender-diverse prisoners; litigation over placement/treatment is recorded without outcome.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National rule places transgender prisoners by gender identity; officers in one province were generally mindful of safety.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Identity-based placement mitigates birth-sex custody exposure, but reported abuse means detention if it occurs remains a serious residual risk.

federal_state_facilities.protection: National human-rights protection for gender identity/expression may cover services, but no bathroom/facility rule or enforcement outcome is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented universal facility exclusion interacts with documents, policing or custody.

care_services.exposure: The substance of one province's shielded 2024 health statutes is not documented; no visitor care denial is documented.
care_services.interaction: Uncertainty matters mainly if a traveller or travelling minor needs emergency or gender-related care; no traveller-facing care rule is established.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: An advocacy source documents a rising organised anti-trans movement; police-reported hate crimes rose six consecutive years, +169% since 2018, but the series is not disaggregated by gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Gender identity/expression are protected in the national human-rights act and criminal-code hate provisions since 2017.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Protection exists on paper and one provincial route is documented, but the dossier does not prove visitor-case remedies change outcomes.

minors_guardians.exposure: One province requires parental consent under 16 for a preferred name/gender identity at school, using an override; another's health/education/sport statutes were shielded by an override.
minors_guardians.protection: A separate province has a 2012 anti-bullying statute covering LGBTQ students, with comparable laws elsewhere.
minors_guardians.interaction: School rules primarily affect resident enrolment, not a visiting minor's short stay; the shielded health statutes leave a travelling-family care question unresolved.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: A 2022 survey found 39% of 2SLGBTQI+ respondents reported identity-based violence over five years, 90% verbal and 17% physical; this is LGBT-wide and dated, so it is only a weak current-prevalence signal.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-motivation provisions provide a reporting/prosecution route; no anti-trans prosecution outcome for a visitor is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Rising reports may reflect hostility and/or reporting, without disaggregation they do not establish a trans-specific visitor violence rate.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Two key publications were not retrievable, border/facility practice and most provinces' document procedures are unsourced, and litigation outcomes are missing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: One province publishes policy and case law under its human-rights code, giving a documented recourse route there.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of traveller-specific evidence in this partly thin dossier is not proof of safety, so the score stays below the strong-protection tier.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.85-A: that anchor documents broad acceptance, audited service correction and convictions; here hate crimes are rising, remedies for visitors are not shown operating, and custody abuse plus provincial minor-related rollbacks remain unresolved.

Similar to 0.75-C: lawful expression, accepted documents, a dead-letter-free protective framework and ordinary-court recourse, with friction and an open custody/placement edge case. Here identity-based custody is stronger, but reported prisoner abuse and organised hostility pull it slightly down.

Higher than 0.55-C: that anchor has repeated visitor harassment/ejections on transport with patchy remedies. Here there is no documented universal exclusion, police targeting, service-denial pattern or facility ban, and formal hate-crime/human-rights recourse is present.

parsed.synthesis: The combined federal-provincial regime protects on paper, accepts identity-based custody and an X marker, and provides at least one documented human-rights route, with no documented traveller-facing universal exposure or organised targeting. The operative risk is therefore conditional: if outed in ordinary visitor settings there is no documented state-imposed exclusion, but rising hate-crime reports, organised anti-trans activity, reported custody abuse and unexplained provincial health/school rollbacks prevent a low-risk rating. For a travelling minor, school-consent law is largely resident-facing; the shielded health statutes are the unresolved family exposure.
